gloss: destination address; recipient address; shipping address

definitions.gloss: destination address; recipient address; shipping address
definitions.explanation: The address to which something is being sent — a package, letter, or shipment. The place or person on the receiving end of a delivery.

examples.japanese: {送|おく}り{先|さき}を{書|か}いてください。
{送|おく}り{先|さき}の{住所|じゅうしょ}が{間違|まちが}っていた。
{送|おく}り{先|さき}を{変更|へんこう}したい{場合|ばあい}は、{発送前|はっそうまえ}にご{連絡|れんらく}ください。
examples.english: If you wish to change the shipping address, please contact us before dispatch.

examples.japanese: この{荷物|にもつ}の{送|おく}り{先|さき}は{自宅|じたく}ではなく{会社|かいしゃ}にしてほしい。
examples.english: I'd like the delivery destination for this package to be my office, not my home.

notes:
Composed of {送|おく}り (sending, from the verb {送|おく}る) and {先|さき} (destination, place ahead). The {先|さき} suffix is productive in Japanese for indicating the destination or counterpart of an action: {届|とど}け{先|さき} (delivery address), {連絡先|れんらくさき} (contact information), {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し{先|さき} (place one is moving to).

You will encounter this word when sending packages at the post office or a convenience store, filling out delivery forms ({伝票|でんぴょう}), or shopping online. Japanese delivery slips typically have fields for both {送|おく}り{先|さき} (recipient) and {依頼主|いらいぬし} or {送|おく}り{主|ぬし} (sender).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {送|おく}り{先|さき}の{住所|じゅうしょ}: recipient's address
- {送|おく}り{先|さき}を{変更|へんこう}する: to change the shipping address
- {送|おく}り{先|さき}を{指定|してい}する: to specify the delivery destination
- {送|おく}り{先|さき}{不明|ふめい}: address unknown (undeliverable)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {届|とど}け{先|さき}: delivery address — a near-synonym, slightly more focused on where something arrives
- {宛先|あてさき}: addressee, destination — used for letters and emails as well as packages
- {差出人|さしだしにん}: sender — the opposite side of the transaction
